newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU crush margins boost soybean imports - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: EU crush margins boost soybean imports - Oil World.

text.p: Soybean imports and processing picked up in the European Union in October and November with attractive crush margins, the independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.

It gave no figures, but said soy oil prices had attractive discounts over rape, sunseed and palm oils -- despite demand-led U.S. soycomplex price rises -- and this resulted in sizeable soy oil exports to third country buyers.
Oil World said soy oil prices could have been expected to fall when big German consumers said they would not use oil from genetically-modified soybeans.

Instead, the controversy boosted the prices of other oils in Europe, with palm oil underpinned by declining seasonal production and strong demand. Soy oil was allowed to follow higher while maintaining a discount.
Oil World was bullish on oilseeds prices, citing tightness.
In an analysis of EU meals output, Oil World said October/June 1995/96 supplies of 35.70 million tonnes were down 2.5 percent from 1994/95, mostly in northwest Europe.
Citing high meal prices versus grains and pulses as well as reductions in pig numbers, Oil World believed an even larger decline in July-September 1996 was likely.
